question: Article 51 of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
option_2: Promotion of international peace and security
option_4: Organization of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promotion of international peace and security.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51 falls under Part IV of the Constitution, i.e., the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).

• It directs the State to promote international peace and security (अंतरराष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा की अभिवृद्धि), maintain just and honourable relations between nations, and encourage settlement of disputes by arbitration.

• It reflects India's commitment to a peaceful foreign policy and principles like Panchsheel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• DPSP (Articles 36–51) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and are non-justiciable.

• Article 51 was strengthened in spirit by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, which also added Fundamental Duties (Article 51A).

• The DPSPs aim to establish a welfare state and social & economic democracy.

NOTE

• Promotion of co-operative societies (Option 1): Relates to Article 43B (added by 97th Amendment, 2011), not Article 51.

• Uniform Civil Code (Option 3): Covered under Article 44 of the DPSP.

• Organization of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry (Option 4): Covered under Article 48 of the DPSP.

question: In September 2024, who has been appointed as Director General of the Narcotics Control Bureau?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anurag Garg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In September 2024, Anurag Garg, a 1993-batch Himachal Pradesh cadre IPS officer, was appointed as the Director General of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB).

• The Narcotics Control Bureau (नारकोटिक्स कंट्रोल ब्यूरो) is the nodal drug law enforcement and intelligence agency of India.

• The appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NCB was established on 17 March 1986 under the NDPS Act, 1985.

• It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and is headquartered in New Delhi.

• The NDPS Act stands for the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.

NOTE

• Sunil Kakkar (Option 1): Not associated with the NCB DG appointment in 2024.

• Rajneet Kohli (Option 2): A corporate executive (associated with Britannia/Coca-Cola India), not the NCB chief.

• Ambuj Chandna (Option 3): A banking sector professional (Kotak Mahindra Bank), unrelated to the NCB.

question: On October 2, 2024, the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan was launched in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On October 2, 2024, PM Narendra Modi launched the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan from Hazaribagh, Jharkhand (झारखंड).

• The scheme aims at the holistic and sustainable development of tribal villages and communities across India.

• The launch coincided with the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi and was linked to the 150th birth anniversary year of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The abhiyan covers around 63,000 tribal-majority villages, benefiting nearly 5 crore tribal people.

• 'Dharti Aaba' means 'Father of the Earth', a title used for tribal icon Birsa Munda.

• The initiative is implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 2): Capital is Patna; not the launch venue of this abhiyan.

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): India's most populous state; not the launch state.

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): Has a large tribal population but was not the launch location.

question: India ranks at what position in the World Competitiveness Index 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 39th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India was ranked 39th in the IMD World Competitiveness Index 2024 (विश्व प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता सूचकांक).

• The index is released annually by the Institute for Management Development (IMD), based in Lausanne, Switzerland.

• It assessed 67 economies in the 2024 edition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The ranking is based on four factors: economic performance, government efficiency, business efficiency, and infrastructure.

• Singapore topped the World Competitiveness Ranking 2024.

• India's rank improved from 40th in 2023 to 39th in 2024.

NOTE

• 46th (Option 1): Not India's rank in this index for 2024.

• 19th (Option 2): Too high a position; not India's rank.

• 61st (Option 3): Incorrect; India was placed 39th, not 61st.

question: The State of the World's Children 2024 report was published by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UNICEF.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The State of the World's Children (SOWC) 2024 report was published by UNICEF (यूनिसेफ).

• The 2024 edition was themed on 'The Future of Childhood in a Changing World', focusing on demographic shifts, climate crises, and frontier technologies.

• It is UNICEF's flagship annual report, first published in 1980.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• UNICEF stands for the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund, established in 1946 and headquartered in New York City, USA.

• Its current Executive Director is Catherine Russell.

• UNICEF won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.

NOTE

• World Bank (Option 2): Publishes the World Development Report, not SOWC.

• IMF (Option 3): Publishes the World Economic Outlook.

• World Economic Forum (Option 4): Publishes the Global Competitiveness Report and Global Gender Gap Report.

question: The Allographa effusosoredica, a newly discovered species in western ghats belong to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is lichen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Allographa effusosoredica, a newly discovered species in the Western Ghats, is a species of lichen (लाइकेन).

• A lichen is a composite organism formed from a symbiotic association between a fungus and an alga or cyanobacterium.

• Lichens are widely used as bio-indicators of air pollution as they are highly sensitive to pollutants.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Western Ghats is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the world's eight 'hottest biodiversity hotspots'.

• The study of lichens is called Lichenology.

• Lichens grow on rocks, tree bark and soil, and can survive in extreme environments.

NOTE

• cat (Option 2): A domesticated mammal of the family Felidae; not the newly discovered species.

• bat (Option 3): The only mammal capable of true flight; unrelated to this discovery.

• butterfly (Option 4): An insect of the order Lepidoptera; not a lichen.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Above Average'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitabha Bagchi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The book 'Above Average' (2007) was written by Indian author Amitabha Bagchi (अमिताभ बागची).

• It is a coming-of-age novel set largely around IIT Delhi and the life of an engineering student.

• Amitabha Bagchi is himself an IIT Delhi computer science professor and alumnus.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Amitabha Bagchi's novel 'Half the Night Is Gone' won the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature 2019.

• His other works include 'The Householder' and 'This Place'.

• 'Above Average' was his debut novel.

NOTE

• Amit Varma (Option 1): Indian writer and podcaster; author of 'My Friend Sancho'.

• Anita Nair (Option 3): Author of 'Ladies Coupé' and 'Mistress'.

• Amish Tripathi (Option 4): Author of the 'Shiva Trilogy' (The Immortals of Meluha).

question: 'Mangal' folk songs are traditional to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Mangal' folk songs are traditional to the state of Uttarakhand (उत्तराखंड).

• These are auspicious/ceremonial songs sung mainly during weddings and religious functions in the Garhwal and Kumaon regions.

• They are part of Uttarakhand's rich tradition of folk music that celebrates life events and rituals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous folk songs/dances of Uttarakhand include Jhora, Chhopati, Chholiya, Thadya and Jhumaila.

• Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh on 9 November 2000.

• Its capital is Dehradun (Gairsain is the summer/declared capital).

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Dekhni, Fugdi and Mando.

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Famous for Lavani and Powada folk traditions.

• Telangana (Option 3): Known for Bathukamma and Perini Shivatandavam.

question: 'Pinjar', a book portraying the trauma of Partition has been written by which Indian author?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amrita Pritam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Pinjar' (The Skeleton) was written by the celebrated Punjabi writer Amrita Pritam (अमृता प्रीतम) in 1950.

• The novel portrays the trauma of the Partition of India (1947) through the story of a Hindu woman, Puro, who is abducted.

• A 2003 Hindi film 'Pinjar' directed by Chandraprakash Dwivedi was based on this novel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Amrita Pritam was the first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956) for her poem 'Sunehe'.

• She was awarded the Jnanpith Award (1981) and the Padma Vibhushan (2004).

• Her famous Partition poem is 'Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu'.

NOTE

• Krishna Sobti (Option 1): Hindi author of 'Zindaginama' and 'Mitro Marjani'.

• Ismat Chughtai (Option 3): Urdu writer known for the short story 'Lihaaf'.

• Mahadevi Verma (Option 4): Hindi poet of the Chhayavaad movement, wrote 'Yama'.

question: Which of the following is a traditional dance associated with the culture of Sikkim?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Snow Lion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Snow Lion dance (also called Singhi Chham) is a traditional dance associated with the culture of Sikkim (सिक्किम).

• It is performed by the Bhutia community and depicts the mythical snow lion, a symbol of the snowy Himalayan ranges, especially Mount Kanchenjunga.

• The dancers wear a furry white-and-blue lion costume during the performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Sikkim include Maruni, Chu Faat, Rechungma and Tashi Yangku.

• Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975.

• Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, is located in Sikkim.

NOTE

• Loor (Option 1): A folk dance of Haryana.

• Dind (Option 2): A folk dance associated with Maharashtra.

• Padhar (Option 3): A folk dance of Gujarat.

question: The most popular argument regarding the origin of the universe is the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Big Bang Theory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The most widely accepted argument regarding the origin of the universe is the Big Bang Theory (बिग बैंग थ्योरी).

• It proposes that the universe began as an extremely hot, dense singularity about 13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.

• The theory was strongly supported by Edwin Hubble's observation of the expanding universe.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The term 'Big Bang' was coined by astronomer Fred Hoyle.

• Belgian priest and physicist Georges Lemaître is regarded as the father of the Big Bang theory.

• The Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR) is considered strong evidence for the Big Bang.

NOTE

• Plate Tectonics (Option 2): A geological theory explaining the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates, not the origin of the universe.

• Quantum Mechanics (Option 3): A branch of physics dealing with the behaviour of matter and energy at atomic/subatomic scales.

• String Theory (Option 4): A theoretical framework proposing that particles are tiny vibrating strings; not the popular origin theory.

question: What does a change in either the speed or direction of an object signify?
option_2: A change in its state of motion
solution_text:
The correct answer is A change in its state of motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A change in either the speed or direction of an object signifies a change in its state of motion (इसकी गति की अवस्था में परिवर्तन).

• Since velocity is a vector quantity (having both magnitude and direction), any change in speed or direction changes the velocity, i.e., the state of motion.

• Such a change requires the application of an external force (as per Newton's First Law of Motion).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A change in the state of motion produces acceleration.

• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia) states that an object continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

• Force is measured in Newton (N) in the SI system.

NOTE

• A change in its mass (Option 1): Mass is the amount of matter and does not change with motion under normal conditions.

• A change in its shape (Option 3): A change in shape indicates deformation, not a change in motion.

• A change in its temperature (Option 4): Temperature relates to thermal energy, not the motion state of the object.

question: Which Indian startup has developed the country's first full-stack 25-qubit quantum computer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is QpiAI.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bengaluru-based startup QpiAI developed India's first full-stack 25-qubit quantum computer, named 'QpiAI-Indus' (April 2025).

• It was launched under India's National Quantum Mission (राष्ट्रीय क्वांटम मिशन).

• It integrates a superconducting quantum processor with an AI-driven software stack.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The National Quantum Mission was approved in 2023 with an outlay of about ₹6,000 crore.

• A qubit (quantum bit) is the basic unit of quantum information, which can exist in superposition of 0 and 1.

• QpiAI was founded by Nagendra Nagaraja.

NOTE

• QNu Labs (Option 2): An Indian quantum-safe cryptography and security startup.

• Prenishq (Option 3): Not associated with developing this quantum computer.

• QuPrayog (Option 4): Not the developer of India's first 25-qubit quantum computer.

question: In the late 1980s, the government of India approached an International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to tackle with the economic crisis, that bank is also known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) is popularly known as the World Bank (विश्व बैंक).

• In the late 1980s and early 1990s, India approached it (and the IMF) to tackle the balance of payments crisis and the economic crisis.

• The IBRD provides loans and financial assistance to member countries for development.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The World Bank was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington, D.C., USA.

• The World Bank Group has five institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID.

• The 1991 crisis led to India's landmark LPG (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) reforms.

NOTE

• Asian Development Bank (Option 2): Established in 1966, headquartered in Manila, Philippines.

• World Trade Bank (Option 3): No such major international institution exists by this exact name.

• Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (Option 4): Established in 2016, headquartered in Beijing, China.

question: As of July 2025, which of the following central public sector enterprise is awarded with "Navratna" status?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers Limited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers Limited (RCF) was granted 'Navratna' status (नवरत्न का दर्जा) by the Department of Public Enterprises.

• RCF became one of the Navratna CPSEs, giving it greater financial and operational autonomy.

• It is a leading fertilizer and chemical manufacturing public sector undertaking.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Navratna status allows a CPSE to make capital investments up to a specified limit without government approval.

• As of the given period, India had a growing list of Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna CPSEs.

• RCF's popular fertilizer brands include 'Ujjwala' and 'Suphala'.

NOTE

• Steel Authority of India Limited (Option 2): SAIL is a Maharatna company, a higher category than Navratna.

• Rural Electrification Corporation Limited (Option 3): REC Ltd is a Maharatna company.

• Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (Option 4): HPCL is a Maharatna company.

question: Which Sikh Guru instituted the Khalsa in 1699?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Gobind Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Gobind Singh (गुरु गोबिंद सिंह), the tenth Sikh Guru, instituted the Khalsa in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi.

• He initiated the first five members, known as the 'Panj Pyare' (Five Beloved Ones).

• He introduced the five Ks (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan) as symbols of Sikh identity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Guru Gobind Singh was born in 1666 at Patna and became Guru after his father's martyrdom.

• He declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.

• He authored the Dasam Granth.

NOTE

• Guru Nanak (Option 1): The first Sikh Guru and founder of Sikhism.

• Guru Ramdas (Option 2): The fourth Guru, who founded the city of Amritsar.

• Guru Tegh Bahadur (Option 3): The ninth Guru, martyred by Aurangzeb; father of Guru Gobind Singh.

question: Which of the following slogans was raised by Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
option_3: "Give Me Blood, and I Shall Give You Freedom."
option_4: "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!"
solution_text:
The correct answer is "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!".

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The slogan "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!" (स्वतंत्रता मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूँगा) was given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

• Tilak was known as 'Lokmanya' and was one of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio of the extremist phase.

• He was among the earliest leaders to demand complete 'Swaraj' (self-rule).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak started the newspapers 'Kesari' (Marathi) and 'Maratha' (English).

• He popularised the public celebrations of Ganesh Utsav and Shivaji Jayanti to unite people.

• He authored 'Gita Rahasya' and 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'.

NOTE

• "Satyamev Jayate" (Option 1): Taken from the Mundaka Upanishad; popularised by Madan Mohan Malaviya.

• "Jai Hind" (Option 2): Slogan associated with Subhas Chandra Bose.

• "Give Me Blood, and I Shall Give You Freedom." (Option 3): Given by Subhas Chandra Bose.

question: Who can dissolve the House of the People of India before its term ends?
option_2: Speaker of the House of the People
solution_text:
The correct answer is President on Prime minister's advice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The House of the People (Lok Sabha) can be dissolved before its term ends by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister (प्रधानमंत्री की सलाह पर राष्ट्रपति).

• This power is exercised under Article 85 of the Constitution.

• The President generally acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Article 74).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years from the date of its first sitting.

• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.

• The Lok Sabha's term can be extended during a National Emergency (one year at a time).

NOTE

• Speaker of the House of the People (Option 2): The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha but cannot dissolve it.

• Chief Justice of India (Option 3): Heads the judiciary; has no power to dissolve the legislature.

• Election Commission (Option 4): Conducts elections but does not dissolve the Lok Sabha.

question: Which of the following crop is NOT associated with dryland farming?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jute (जूट) is NOT associated with dryland farming, as it requires high rainfall, high humidity and standing water.

• Dryland farming is practised in regions with low and erratic rainfall (below 75 cm) without irrigation.

• Jute is a moisture-loving crop, mainly grown in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• West Bengal is the largest producer of jute in India.

• Jute is known as the 'Golden Fibre'.

• Dryland crops are typically hardy, drought-resistant coarse cereals and pulses.

NOTE

• Guar (Option 1): A drought-resistant legume well suited to dryland/arid farming.

• Bajra (Option 2): Pearl millet, a typical dryland/rainfed crop grown in arid regions.

• Ragi (Option 4): Finger millet, a hardy dryland cereal crop.

question: What was the main purpose of land reforms in India post independence?
option_1: To change in the ownership of landholdings.
option_3: To increase foreign direct investment in agriculture.
option_4: To sell all the landholdings to private companies for better compliance
solution_text:
The correct answer is To change in the ownership of landholdings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main purpose of land reforms in post-independence India was to bring about a change in the ownership of landholdings (भूमि जोतों के स्वामित्व में परिवर्तन).

• The reforms aimed to abolish intermediaries (like Zamindars) and transfer land to the actual tillers.

• The objective was to ensure social justice and equitable distribution of agricultural land.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The main components of land reforms were: abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms, ceiling on landholdings, and consolidation of holdings.

• 'Land to the tiller' was a key slogan of these reforms.

• The Bhoodan Movement by Vinoba Bhave complemented land reform efforts.

NOTE

• To increase urbanisation (Option 2): Not the aim of land reforms, which focused on agrarian/rural structure.

• To increase foreign direct investment in agriculture (Option 3): FDI was not the objective of post-independence land reforms.

• To sell all the landholdings to private companies (Option 4): Contrary to the goal of distributing land to tillers.

question: Child Budgeting was first time adopted by government of India in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008-09.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Child Budgeting (चाइल्ड बजट) was first adopted by the Government of India in 2008-09.

• It refers to the analysis of budgetary allocations meant specifically for the welfare and development of children (below 18 years).

• It ensures transparency and accountability in spending on children's needs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Child Budgeting focuses on sectors such as child health, education, development and protection.

• It is a tool similar in concept to Gender Budgeting, which India adopted in 2005-06.

• The Ministry of Women and Child Development is a key implementing ministry.

NOTE

• 2001-02 (Option 1): Not the year Child Budgeting was first introduced.

• 2013-14 (Option 2): Incorrect; Child Budgeting predates this year.

• 1991-92 (Option 3): The year of major economic reforms (LPG), not Child Budgeting.

question: Which of the following deficit includes only such transactions that affect the current income and expenditure of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Revenue deficit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue deficit (राजस्व घाटा) includes only those transactions that affect the current income and expenditure of the government.

• It is the excess of the government's total revenue expenditure over its total revenue receipts.

• Formula: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A high revenue deficit indicates that the government is borrowing to meet consumption/current needs.

• The FRBM Act, 2003 aimed to reduce revenue and fiscal deficits.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• Primary deficit (Option 1): Fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

• Trade deficit (Option 3): Excess of imports over exports; relates to external trade, not government income/expenditure.

• Fiscal deficit (Option 4): Excess of total expenditure over total receipts (excluding borrowings).

question: How is air initially filtered when it is taken into the human body?
option_1: By fine hair in the nostrils
solution_text:
The correct answer is By fine hair in the nostrils.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Air is initially filtered by the fine hair present in the nostrils (नाक में बारीक बाल), called cilia/vibrissae.

• These hairs and the mucus trap dust, dirt and microbes, preventing them from reaching the lungs.

• This is the first line of defence of the respiratory system.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The nasal cavity also warms and moistens the incoming air.

• The pathway of air is: nostrils → nasal cavity → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → lungs.

• The exchange of gases occurs in the alveoli of the lungs.

NOTE

• By tonsils in the throat (Option 2): Tonsils help fight infection but are not the initial air filter.

• By rings of cartilage (Option 3): C-shaped cartilage rings keep the trachea open; they do not filter air.

• By the lungs (Option 4): The lungs are the site of gas exchange, not initial filtration.

question: What of the following statement is correct regarding phloem of a plant? I. The translocation in phloem is achieved by utilizing energy. II. Material are transferred into phloem tissue using energy from ATP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both statements are correct: translocation in phloem (फ्लोएम) is an active process that utilises energy.

• Materials (like sucrose) are loaded into the phloem tissue using energy from ATP, which increases the osmotic pressure and moves water in.

• This pressure difference moves material from source to sink (pressure-flow / mass-flow hypothesis).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Phloem transports food (sugars) and can move it in both directions (bidirectional).

• Phloem is made of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

• Xylem, in contrast, transports water and minerals upward and is a largely passive, unidirectional process.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, since statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, since statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both statements accurately describe phloem translocation.

question: According to Jaina ethics, the vow of 'aparigraha' refers to ______.
option_4: non-possession of things more than one's requirement
solution_text:
The correct answer is non-possession of things more than one's requirement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Jaina ethics, 'Aparigraha' (अपरिग्रह) refers to non-possession / non-attachment, i.e., not acquiring things beyond one's requirement.

• It is one of the five vows (Pancha Mahavrata) of Jainism.

• It teaches control over greed and limiting material possessions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The five vows of Jainism are: Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession) and Brahmacharya (celibacy).

• The vow of Brahmacharya was added by the 24th Tirthankara Mahavira; the other four came from Parshvanatha.

• Jainism's core principle is Ahimsa (non-violence).

NOTE

• fasting until death (Option 1): This refers to 'Sallekhana' or 'Santhara', not Aparigraha.

• refraining from theft (Option 2): This is the vow of 'Asteya'.

• speaking only the truth (Option 3): This is the vow of 'Satya'.
